Hello all,

I have a Shiny app - available under https://owid.shinyapps.io/WortschatzZeit/ - that disconnects quite often. It doesn't happen when I test in on the local desktop. Here is what I checked:

Browser console: There is actually a message saying that it disconnected:
Sat Oct 01 2016 15:11:14 GMT+0200 (CEST): Connection closed. Info: {"type":"close","code":1000,"reason":"Normal closure","wasClean":true}

But "normal closure" does not help me very much.

I am on a starter plan with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and checked if the app uses too much memory. However, memory usage peaks at 300 MB, which should be fine. Also, the log (using showLogs() does not contain any information about errors or warnings. The disconnect is reproducible if you type 1 into the first numericInput widget (labelled "Mindestfrequenz im Ausgangsjahr").

Any help is much appreciated, thank you!

Dear collegues,
I now tried another way to automatically deploy my app but also failed. I do not know what is wrong here because normally my apps are working quite well. I now tried to deploy the app via console completely so that I can deploy the entire app every night to update the daily files.

Again the app is perferctly to deploy from R Studio but not from the console. I tried all possible ways (including a simple app from the net) but always get the same error when I try to deploy the app by a batchfile via the console:

Preparing to deploy document...DONE
Uploading bundle for document: 130102...
Load package: rsconnect
Error in contrib.url(repos, type) :
  trying to use CRAN without setting a mirror
Calling: deployApp ... withCallingHandlers -> <Anonymous> -> available.packages -> contrib.url
Execution stopped.

The web say quite clearly that in the case of deployment via the console the packages have to installed separately and the repository has to be named what I did.
My code (deploy_test.R) for deployment which I call from a batchfile ("C:\Program Files\R\R-3.3.1\bin\Rscript.exe" "C:\AABackup\Shiny\code\deploy_test.R") is:

setwd("C:/AABackup/Shiny/code/test") #the app is in that directory
install.packages("shiny", repos="https://cran.rstudio.com/")
library(shiny)
install.packages("rsconnect", repos="https://cran.rstudio.com/")
library(rsconnect)

rsconnect::setAccountInfo(name='cosyna-nodes', token='431669DA29#######', secret='Qf32ulpnqTOe########')

deployApp(appDir = getwd(), appFiles = NULL, appFileManifest = NULL,
          appPrimaryDoc = "test.R", appSourceDoc = NULL, appName = NULL,
          contentCategory = NULL, account = NULL, server = NULL, upload = TRUE,
          launch.browser = getOption("rsconnect.launch.browser", interactive()),
          quiet = FALSE, lint = TRUE, metadata = list())

messages.subject: Re: Problems with dropbox file download within shiny.io

messages.body_plain:
I have solved the problem:

The below error message can be avoided when putting the line

chooseCRANmirror(ind = ###,useHTTPS = getOption("useHTTPS", TRUE), local.only = TRUE)

before the deployApp line.

the value for ind = ### can be chosen in the local cran list on the respective computer where R is running. This file is in the folder C:\Program Files\R\R-3.3.1\doc and is named CRAN_mirrors.csv. The value for ind is the line number where the repository is listed in that file.

Al the best
Philipp

messages.body_plain:
Philipp,
shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> runs on Linux.  We tried to add instructions in the docs <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/> to explain that you don't want to be using absolute paths, and to be aware that although you could build your shiny application on any of the supported R versions, it will be recreated on a linux environment on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

-Tareef

On Sun, Oct 9, 2016 at 3:46 AM, Philipp Fischer <philipp...@awi.de> wrote:

> I have solved the problem:
>
> The below error message can be avoided when putting the line
>
> chooseCRANmirror(ind = ###,useHTTPS = getOption("useHTTPS", TRUE), local.only = TRUE)
>
> before the deployApp line.
>
> the value for ind = ### can be chosen in the local cran list on the respective computer where R is running. This file is in the folder C:\Program Files\R\R-3.3.1\doc and is named CRAN_mirrors.csv. The value for ind is the line number where the repository is listed in that file.
>
> Al the best
> Philipp

Thanks for your willingness to help.  I have the three text files of ngrams.  They are a total of 6MB.  The three files are loaded into the environment as the first three lines of the server function.  They are read in via a basic read.csv command

All I am doing is accepting textInput and then using a simple function to recommend the top three next words. The function returns a list of three words.  I have to call the function three times as i have not been able to determine how to extract elements of a list that is called by a reactive function. messages.subject: Is my data safe in shinyapps
messages.subject_clean: Is my data safe in shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
Dear shiny users,

I made an app in which the user can upload a datafile to use. It is basically a data analytics tool. Now I am hosting it on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> where of course it is accessible to all.
My concern is not actually about the app being accessible for everyone, but rather with the data of the user.
Are the users of my app risking their (possibly confidential) data?

I would be glad to hear more about this!

With kind regards,

Pieter

messages.body_snippet:
Andrew I suspect you pulled a version of dplyr from GitHub that didn't express the dependency upon plogr properly, could you remove the package and re-install it and see if that helps?

On Thursday, O

messages.subject: How to use our R package in Shinyspps?
messages.subject_clean: How to use our R package in Shinyspps?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm very new to Shinyapps and R. I'm actually helping my wife out here. She has her R package and now wants to make an interactive website out of it. How can we do it? Is there any step-by-step tutorial (preferably video tutorial) that anyone knows? Any help is much appreciated.

Thank you,
--Ishti

") bbb } #做一个循坏开始跑数 final<-data.table() for (i in 1:10){ final<-rbind(final,readdata(i)) print(i) } library('shiny') server<-function(input, output, session) { output$yi <- renderText({ HTML(transfer_html_table(rawdata= final %>% filter(价格<=1))) }) output$er <- renderText({ HTML(transfer_html_table(rawdata=final %>% filter(价格>1 & 价格<=2))) }) output$san <- renderText({ HTML(transfer_html_table(rawdata=final %>% filter(价格>2 & 价格<=5))) }) output$si <- renderText({ HTML(transfer_html_table(rawdata=final %>% filter(价格>5))) }) } ui<-fluidPage( titlePanel('亚马逊Kindle今日特价书总结'), mainPanel( tabsetPanel( tabPanel("低于1元特价书",htmlOutput("yi")), tabPanel("1-2元特价书",htmlOutput("er")), tabPanel("2-5元特价书",htmlOutput("san")), tabPanel("5元以上特价书",htmlOutput("si")) ) ) ) shinyApp(ui=ui,server=server)

Thanks Tareef once again. After reading the first written tutorial and reading some blogs, I've finally just now was able to publish our R app to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, thanks for your tips.

Few notes/experience to share:
Had to change our R package output to dataTable format from text to get a meaningful result in the UI
Had to upload our code to GitHub and use devTools::install_github('path-to-our-repository') to install our created R package to Shinyapps, local copies of the files wouldn't work. Got the tip from: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/l6nug9hMh7g
Thanks!
--Ishti
